set.st: A Norwegian who died at the county poor farm in Oct 1901 said loot from an 1870 Trondhjem bank robbery was buried under the floor of his little wood-turning shop near a sunken gas pipe, on a strip near the Muskegon Lake shore, then the edge of town, across the street from the electric light plant. From Dec 1902 a man leased the lot and dug 8 ft down under the floors; no find reported. Urban: look-only. Pin is the shop block on old N. Terrace St, not the spot itself.
set.t: Shop stood on old N. Terrace St across from the 1880s electric light works, near the lake; the 1903 dig went 8 ft down under the floor with no find. Urban: look-only.
set.pl: Old N. Terrace St (pre-realignment line), opposite the electric light works mid-block between Market and Lake Sts, Muskegon (1887 Sanborn sheet 7)
pinev: Block-level: the 1887 Sanborn sheet 7 shows the electric light works on the E side of N. Terrace St mid-block between Market and Lake Sts, with a woodworking shop opposite on the W side; the 1901 obituary puts the turning shop on N. Terrace St and the 1903 feature puts it across from the lighting plant. Measured on the old street line; the circle covers both sides (about 150 m).

src: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Muskegon (1887), sheet 7 (Library of Congress)
